newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas sees rise in 1997 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Havas sees rise in 1997 net profit.

text.p: Havas expects to make a 1997 net profit, before goodwill writedowns, of 1.5 billion francs against an expected 1.2 billion in 1996, finance director Nicolas Duhamel told an analysts' briefing.

He added that after a series of corporate transaction concerning the buy-out of minorities in CEP Communication, the acquisition of an additional stake in Canal Plus and other activities from Generale des Eaux, the company's net consolidated debt would be about three billion francs.
It made a 1995 net profit of 1.112 billion francs.
Before these operations the Havas debt was slighlty below 500 million francs.
In 1997, the debt-to-equity ratio will go to 21 percent from less than five percent and the shareholders funds to 14.1 billion francs from 12.8 billion.
Consolidated cash flow will reach 3.2 billion, against two billion before the operations.
The number of shares in Havas will rise to 79.95 million from 64.2 million.
Earnings per share are seen at 18.8 francs in 1997 from 18.7 francs in 1996 and 17.5 in 1995.
